audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Skill/Skill/Skill/Gnar/Skill/Gnar/Gnar while the content whys[] beside them said the opposite on five rows — 'Gnar's level-1 boomerang... poke you freely', 'Level 3 E Facebreaker gives you a reliable stun', 'Through 4-5 your sustained damage... beat his Mini-form trades', 'With a first item you out-brawl Mini Gnar', 'skilled Mega play brings the matchup back to even'.
audit.why: The mirror (gnar__sett) settled rows 0, 2, 3, 5 and 6 as Gnar/Sett/Sett/Sett/Skill and the packet chart agrees on every one of them. Rows 1 and 4 the mirror left as Skill, so I did not reopen them.
audit.corrected: win[0]=Gnar, win[2]=Sett, win[3]=Sett, win[5]=Sett, win[6]=Skill with the matching phases[N].side, proposed as one atomic group; ratings moved with them and phases[2], [3], [5], [6] whys restated to the new owners.

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldown appeared anywhere, so 'punish him between hops' had nothing behind it.
audit.why: Gnar's Hop is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s — the longest escape cooldown in the lane and the reason Mini Gnar is catchable at all once Facebreaker (16s at rank 1) is up. The Show Stopper is 120s at rank 1 and Haymaker 18s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Hop's 22s at rank 1 keyed to the Levels 4-5 and first-item lines, Facebreaker's 16s to the level-3 spike, R's 120s to the level-6 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (a) Facebreaker was called a 'reliable stun' with no mention that it only stuns with enemies on opposite sides — against a lone Gnar it is a slow he simply hops out of. (b) Haymaker was described as healing ('your W heal chunk him') — it grants a shield, not a heal, and its true damage is centre-only. (c) The mid text called Sett's Q a slow; Knuckle Down is two empowered punches plus move speed toward enemies, and Sett's slow comes from a one-sided E.
audit.why: Riot's Sett E text: 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' Riot's Sett W text: 'gain a shield and punch an area, dealing true damage in the center and physical damage on the sides.' Riot's Sett Q text has no slow clause. The mirror recorded (a) and (b) identically, so both sides now match.
audit.corrected: Level-3 spike now tells the player to pull Gnar into the minions so the E stuns rather than slows; the first-item spike replaces 'W heal' with the shield-plus-damage cash; mid text names Knuckle Down's move speed instead of a phantom slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] read 'To poke with Q boomerang and hop away on W' — Hop is Gnar's E. In Mini form W is Hyper, a passive damage-and-move-speed stack, not an escape.
audit.why: A player tracking the wrong slot waits out the wrong cooldown: Hyper is 7s, Hop is 22s at rank 1. The entire punish window depends on knowing which one he just spent.

edits.before: Facebreaker is online — the E-stun into double punch + W is your full pattern. Run it the moment Gnar burns GNAR! (Mega Stun).
edits.after: Facebreaker (16s) is online, but it only stuns with a target on each side — pull Gnar into your minions, not away from them, then punch and cash W.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Gnar has his core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield his return damage, out.
edits.after: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier and Mini Gnar cannot brawl back. Punish every boomerang step-up — his Hop is 22s at rank 1 and it is his only exit.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Gnar. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the next trade before he matches your item.
edits.after: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Gnar, whose Hop is 22s at rank 1. Force the trade while he is Mini and has no answer in melee.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track GNAR! (Mega Stun) and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Sterak's makes your all-in unburstable, but the Rage bar decides fights: cash max-grit W with him dead-centre, and never stand near a wall in Mega.

edits.before: Once you have E Facebreaker, wait for Gnar to boomerang (Q) or hop in with W range and pull him into you for a stun, then Q slow and W the empowered swing before he can kite back out.
edits.after: Once Facebreaker (16s) is up, catch him after Boomerang Throw and pull him into your minions — with a target on each side it stuns, alone it only slows. Then double-punch and cash Haymaker.

edits.before: Your R The Show Stopper is a hard answer to Mini Gnar and a great counter to Mega Gnar's Q/W chain — flip him toward your tower and dump W to punish any all-in he tries at Rage-bar.
edits.after: The Show Stopper (120s at rank 1) answers a fleeing Mini and a committing Mega alike — carry him toward your tower, then cash Haymaker with him dead-centre where the panel is true damage.

edits.before: With a completed bruiser item you out-brawl Mini Gnar cleanly; Grit stacks from his pokes let your W heal chunk him whenever he steps up to hit a Q boomerang.
edits.after: With a completed bruiser item you out-brawl Mini Gnar cleanly — his poke only banks Grit, and Haymaker (18s at rank 1) cashes it as a shield plus damage every time he steps up.

edits.before: From 3 on your E Facebreaker pull and Q slow let you catch Mini Gnar; punish every time he steps in for a Q, and use R to shut down Mega all-ins near your side.
edits.after: From 3 your Facebreaker pull and Knuckle Down's move speed let you catch Mini Gnar; punish every step-up for a boomerang, and save R for a Mega all-in on your side.

edits.before: To poke with Q boomerang and hop away on W
edits.after: To poke with Q boomerang and hop away on E

notes: The mirror flagged a data discrepancy worth repeating: this brief's header says games 1880 and win rate 50.27, while the gnar__sett packet reported 767 games at 49.54%. The two packets disagree about the same matchup and someone should reconcile them before either number is shown to a paying user. Rows 1 and 4 stay Skill because the mirror left them there, even though the packet chart reads Sett on both — flagged rather than flipped, since reopening a row the mirror settled would put the two directions back into conflict. Also noted by the mirror: Sett's R carries a derived 'grounding' flag that Riot's description does not support, so I asserted nothing about grounding here.
